ILLUSTRATIVE TARIFF SHEETS FOR  
INTERIM NITS, FIRM CONTRACT DEMAND  
AND NON-FIRM CONTRACT DEMAND 
TRANSMISSION SERVICE RATES
Redlines to PJM Illustrative Tariff Records from February 23, 2026 
Initial Brief 
Tariff, Part XI. Transmission Services Available for Eligible Customers Taking Service on 
Behalf of Co-Located Loads 
Subpart A – Interim Network Integration Transmission Service 
*** 
706 Rates and Charges 
Eligible Customers taking Interim Network Integration Transmission Service shall pay the charges 
set forth in this Section 706. 
706.1 Monthly Demand Charge 
[Reserved] 
Eligible Customer shall pay a monthly Demand Charge for Zone Network Load and Non-Zone 
Network Load, which shall be determined as follows:  Eligible Customer’s measured demand 
amount (in MWs) multiplied by the applicable zonal Network Integration Transmission Service 
rate established pursuant to Section 34.1. 
Revenue Crediting.  Each month, revenue credits will be applied to the gross Monthly Demand 
Charge to determine the actual charge to the Transmission Customer.  Revenue credits shall be 
calculated based on the sum of a Zone’s share of revenues collected during the month from:  (i) 
the Grid Reliance Charge under Schedule [GRC]; and (ii) the Non-Firm Contract Demand Charge 
under Schedule [NFCD].  The sum of these revenues will appear as a reduction to the gross 
monthly rate stated above on a Transmission Customer’s bill in that month for service under this 
schedule.   
706.2 Redispatch Charge 
The Eligible Customer and each Transmission Owner shall pay any redispatch costs as set forth in 
Tariff, Attachment K.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 2 of 17 
706.3 Stranded Cost Recovery 
Any Transmission Owner may seek to recover stranded costs from the Eligible Customer pursuant 
to this Tariff in accordance with the terms, conditions and procedures set forth in FERC Order No. 
888.  However, the Transmission Owner must separately file any proposal to recover stranded 
costs under section 205 of the Federal Power Act. 
706.4 Other Charges 
Eligible Customer shall pay administrative services charges under Tariff, Schedule 1A; Tariff, 
Schedule 9; and Tariff, Schedule 10, consistent with the charges assessed to loads taking Network 
Integration Transmission Service. 
Eligible Customer shall pay Ancillary Services charges in accordance with Tariff, Part I, section 
3. 
Eligible Customer shall pay Black Start Service charges in accordance with Tariff, Schedule 6A.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 3 of 17 
714 Rates and Charges for Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service 
Eligible Customers taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service shall pay the charges set 
forth in this Section 714. 
714.1 Monthly Demand Charge 
[Reserved] 
Eligible Customer shall pay a Monthly Demand Charge based on the Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service amount (MW), as specified in Eligible Customer’s Service Agreement, in 
accordance with Tariff, Schedule [FCD]. 
714.2 Network Upgrade Charge 
[Reserved] 
714.3 Redispatch Charge 
The Eligible Customer and each Transmission Owner shall pay any redispatch costs as set forth in 
Tariff, Attachment K. 
714.4 Stranded Cost Recovery 
Any Transmission Owner may seek to recover stranded costs from the Eligible Customer pursuant 
to this Tariff in accordance with the terms, conditions and procedures set forth in FERC Order No. 
888.  However, the Transmission Owner must separately file any proposal to recover stranded 
costs under section 205 of the Federal Power Act. 
714.5 Other Charges 
Eligible Customer shall pay administrative services charges under Tariff, Schedule 1A; Tariff, 
Schedule 9; and Tariff, Schedule 10 based on the total quantity of MWHs of energy delivered 
using Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, except in the case of any capacity-related 
charges under these schedules, which shall be based on the Eligible Customer’s Unforced Capacity 
Obligation. 
Eligible Customer shall pay Ancillary Services charges, except for Regulation, based on the total 
quantity in MWhs of energy delivered to the Co-Located Load using Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service in accordance with Tariff, Part I, section 3. 
Eligible Customer shall pay Black Start Service charges based on the gross demand Co-Located 
Gross Demand of the Co-Located Load in accordance with Tariff, Schedule 6A. 
Eligible Customer shall pay Regulation charges based on the gross demand Co-Located Gross 
Demand of the Co-Located Load.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 4 of 17 
Eligible Customer shall pay a Grid Reliance Charge based on the Co-Located Gross Demand in 
excess of the Eligible Customer’s Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service amount, in 
accordance with Tariff, Schedule [GRC].  Eligible Customer’s Co-Located Gross Demand and 
Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service amount shall be those contained in Eligible 
Customer’s Service Agreement for Contract Demand Transmission Service.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 5 of 17 
715 Rates and Charges for Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service 
Eligible Customers taking Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service shall pay the charges 
set forth in this Section 715. 
715.1 Monthly Demand Charge 
[Reserved] 
Eligible Customer shall pay a maximum Monthly Demand Charge based on its Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service amount (MW), as specified in Eligible Customer’s Service 
Agreement, in accordance with Tariff, Schedule [NFCD]. 
715.2 Redispatch Charge 
The Eligible Customer and each Transmission Owner shall pay any redispatch costs as set forth in 
Tariff, Attachment K. 
715.3 Stranded Cost Recovery 
Any Transmission Owner may seek to recover stranded costs from the Eligible Customer pursuant 
to this Tariff in accordance with the terms, conditions and procedures set forth in FERC Order No. 
888.  However, the Transmission Owner must separately file any proposal to recover stranded 
costs under section 205 of the Federal Power Act. 
715.4 Other Charges 
Eligible Customer shall pay administrative services charges under Tariff, Schedule 1A; Tariff, 
Schedule 9; and Tariff, Schedule 10 based on the total quantity of MWhs of energy delivered using 
Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, except any capacity-related charges under 
these schedules will not apply. 
Eligible Customer shall pay Ancillary Services charges, except for Regulation, based on the total 
quantity in MWhs of energy delivered to the Co-Located Load using Non-Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service in accordance with Tariff, Part I, section 3. 
To the extent the Eligible Customer does not have an effective Service Agreement for Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service, Eligible Customer shall pay Black Start Service charges 
based on the its Co-Located Gross Demand gross demand of the Co-Located Loadin accordance 
with Tariff, Schedule 6A. 
To the extent the Eligible Customer does not have an effective Service Agreement for Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service, Eligible Customer shall pay Regulation charges based on 
its Co-Located Gross Demand a gross demand of the Co-Located Load.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 6 of 17 
New Proposed Rate Schedules
SCHEDULE [FCD] 
Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service 
For Co-Located Load 
1) 
Eligible Customer taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service in a Zone in which 
Network Integration Transmission Service rates are determined based on formula rates set forth in 
Attachment H shall pay a Monthly Demand Charge based on the Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service Amount (MW), as specified in Eligible Customer’s Service Agreement, 
which shall be determined as follows: 
MDC = FCDTSA X RTZ/12 
Where: 
MDC is the monthly demand charge 
FCDTSA is the Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service Amount (MW), as specified 
in Eligible Customer’s Service Agreement  
RTZ is the rate for Network Integration Transmission Service from Attachment H for the 
Zone in which the Eligible Customer’s Co-Located Load is located, stated in dollars per 
megawatt per year.  For purposes of establishing the RTZ component in the relevant 
Attachment H, the annual peak of the Zone shall be based on the sum of Network Customer 
Loads in the Zone and Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service Amounts for all 
Eligible Customers taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service in the Zone for 
the applicable peak period. 
2) 
Eligible Customers taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service in a Zone in which 
Network Integration Transmission Service rates are not established based on formula rates shall 
pay a Monthly Demand Charge based on the Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service Amount 
(MW), as specified in Eligible Customer’s Service Agreement, multiplied by a Zonal-specific Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service rate filed with FERC pursuant to Section 205 of the 
Federal Power Act.  Those rates will be posted on Transmission Provider’s website. 
3) 
Revenue Crediting.  Each month, credits will be applied to the Eligible Customer’s gross 
Monthly Demand Charge stated above associated with revenue collected from: (i) Grid Reliance 
Charges in accordance with Schedule [GRC]; and (ii) Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service Charges in accordance with Schedule [NFCD], based on each  Eligible Customer’s pro 
rata share of the Zone’s annual peak load, from the most recent 12-month period ending October 
31.  The Eligible Customer’s pro rata share shall be based on the ratio of its Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service Amount during the peak period to the sum of Network Customer Loads in 
the Zone and Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service Amounts for all Eligible Customers 
taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service in the Zone for the applicable peak period.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 7 of 17 
The sum of these revenue credits will appear as a reduction to the gross monthly rate stated above 
on a Eligible Customer’s bill in that month for service under this schedule.   
4) 
Transmission Enhancement Charges.  In addition to the rates set forth in section (1) of 
this Schedule and any other applicable charges, the Eligible Customer shall also pay any 
Transmission Enhancement Charges for which it is designated as a Responsible Customer 
under Schedule 12 appended to the Tariff. 
5)  
Determination of Monthly Charges for ComEd Zone.  On a monthly basis, revenue 
credits shall be calculated based on the sum of ComEd's share of revenues collected during the 
month from: (i) the PJM Border Rate under Schedule 7; (ii) Network Integration Transmission 
Service to Non-Zone 
Network 
Load under Attachment 
H-A; 
(iii) 
Seams 
Elimination 
Charge/Cost Adjustment/Assignment (“SECA”) revenues allocable to ComEd under the Tariff; 
and (iv) any Point-To-Point Transmission Service where the Point of Receipt and the Point of 
Delivery are both internal to the ComEd Zone.  On this basis, the sum of these revenues will appear 
as a reduction to the gross monthly rate stated above on a Transmission Customer’s1 bill in that 
month for service under this schedule. 
6)  
Determination of Monthly Charges for AEP Zone.  On a monthly basis, revenue credits 
shall be calculated based on the sum of AEP’s share of revenues collected during the month from: 
(i) the PJM Border Rate under Schedule 7; (ii) Network Integration Transmission Service to Non-
Zone Network Load under Attachment H-A; and (iii) Firm Point-To-Point Transmission 
Service where the Point of Delivery is internal to the AEP Zone.  The sum of these revenue credits 
will appear as an adjustment (reduction) to the gross monthly rate stated above on a Eligible 
Customer's bill in that month for service under this schedule. 
7)  
Other Supporting Facilities and Taxes.  In addition to the charges set forth in section (1) 
of this schedule, the Eligible Customer shall pay charges determined on a case-by-case basis for 
facilities necessary to provide Transmission Service at voltages lower than those shown 
in Attachment H for the applicable Zone(s) and any amounts necessary to reimburse 
the Transmission Provider for any amounts payable as sales, excise, "Btu," carbon, value-added 
or similar taxes (other than taxes based upon or measured by net income) with respect to the 
amounts payable pursuant to the Tariff.  
1/ Transmission Customer is defined as an Eligible Customer that executes a Service Agreement, 
or requests PJM file an unexecuted Service Agreement, to receive transmission service under the 
Tariff.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 8 of 17 
SCHEDULE [NFCD] 
Non-Firm Contract Demand Service 
For Co-Located Load 
1)
Eligible Customer taking Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service in a Zone in 
which Network Integration Transmission Service rates are determined based on formula rates set 
forth in Attachment H shall pay for such service based on the amount of Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service reserved by the Eligible Customer in MW, multiplied by the 
following rates based on the reservation term: 
Monthly Rate ($/MW): Maximum of the Zonal Firm Contract Demand Transmission Rate (RTZ) 
as calculated pursuant to Schedule [FCD], divided by 12. 
Weekly Rate ($/MW): Maximum of the Zonal Firm Contract Demand Transmission Rate (RTZ) 
as calculated pursuant to Schedule [FCD], divided by 52. 
Daily On-Peak Rate1 ($/MW): Weekly Rate divided by 5. 
Daily Off-Peak Rate2 ($/MW): Weekly Rate divided by 7. 
Hourly On-Peak Rate3 ($/MWh): Maximum of the Zonal Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Rate (RTZ) as calculated pursuant to Schedule [FCD], divided by 4160. 
Hourly Off-Peak Rate4 ($/MWh): Maximum of the Zonal Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Rate (RTZ) as calculated pursuant to Schedule [FCD], divided by 8760. 
1/ Monday–Friday except the following holidays: New Years Day, Memorial Day, Independence 
Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day. 
2/ Saturday and Sunday and the following holidays: New Years Day, Memorial Day, 
Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day. 
3/ 7:00 a.m. up to the hour ending 11:00 p.m. 
4/ 11:00 p.m. up to the hour ending 7:00 a.m. 
The Grid Reliance Charge charged to the Eligible Customer pursuant to Schedule [GRC] will be 
subtracted from the Eligible Customer’s Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service 
Charge on a MWh basis for each MWh of Non-Firm Contract Demand Service included in Eligible 
Customer’s transmission service reservation. 
2) 
Eligible Customers taking Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service in a Zone in 
which Network Integration Transmission Service rates are not established based on formula rates 
shall pay for Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service based on the amount of Non-Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service reserved by the Eligible Customer in MW, multiplied by 
Zonal-specific Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service rates filed with FERC pursuant

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 9 of 17 
to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act.  Those rates will be posted on Transmission Provider’s 
website. 
3) 
Discounts.  Three principal requirements apply to discounts for Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service as follows: (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission 
Provider must be announced to all Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any 
customer-initiated requests for discounts (including requests for use by one’s wholesale merchant 
or an Affiliate’s use) must occur solely by posting on OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated, 
details must be immediately posted on the OASIS.  For any discount agreed to by  Transmission 
Provider, Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted transmission service rate for the 
same time period to all Eligible Customers taking Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service. 
4) 
Transmission Enhancement Charges.  In addition to the rates set forth in section (1) of 
this Schedule and any other applicable charges, the Eligible Customer shall also pay any 
Transmission Enhancement Charges for which it is designated as a Responsible Customer 
under Schedule 12 appended to the Tariff based on the Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service reserved by the Eligible Customer in MW. 
5) 
Revenue Crediting.  Revenues collected from Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service Charges shall be credited to Eligible Customers taking Network Integration Transmission 
Service, Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, and Firm Point-to-Point Transmission 
Service based on each Eligible Customer’s pro rata share of the Zone’s annual peak load based on 
the most recent 12-month period ending October 31.  The Eligible Customer’s pro rata share shall 
be based on the ratio of its Zone Network Load or Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service 
Amount to the sum of Network Customer Loads in the Zone and Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service Amounts for all Eligible Customers taking Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service in the Zone, for the applicable peak period.  The sum of these revenue credits 
will appear as a reduction to the gross monthly rate for Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service on a Eligible Customer’s bill in that month. 
6) 
Other Supporting Facilities and Taxes.  In addition to the charges set forth in section (1) 
of this schedule, the Eligible Customer shall pay charges determined on a case-by-case basis for 
facilities necessary to provide Transmission Service at voltages lower than those shown 
in Attachment H for the applicable Zone(s) and any amounts necessary to reimburse 
the Transmission Provider for any amounts payable as sales, excise, “Btu,” carbon, value-added 
or similar taxes (other than taxes based upon or measured by net income) with respect to the 
amounts payable pursuant to the Tariff.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 10 of 17 
SCHEDULE [GRC] 
Grid Reliance Charge for  
Firm and Non-Firm Contract Demand Service 
For Co-Located Load 
Eligible Customers taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service and Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service shall pay the Grid Reliance Charge for the Zone in which the Point 
of Delivery for the Eligible Customer’s Co-Located Load is located. 
1)  
For Zones in which Transmission Owners in which the Network Integrated Transmission 
Service charge is set pursuant to a formula rate, the Grid Reliance Charge shall be an annual charge 
equal to the Zonal Grid Reliance Rate multiplied by the difference between the Eligible 
Customer’s Co-Located Gross Demand and its Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service 
Amount, both as specified in its service agreement for Firm Contract Demand Service.  For those 
Zones that include multiple Transmission Owners or Transmission Owners with multiple formula 
rate revenue requirements that comprise the total Zonal Rate, the inputs from each relevant formula 
rate revenue requirement and components thereof will be aggregated to determine the 
Transmission Owners relevant expenses and costs used as inputs to the Zonal Grid Reliance Rate, 
as set forth below. 
For each such Zone, the Zonal Grid Reliance Rate shall be calculated as: 
(The Zonal Network Integration Transmission Service Rate X the Grid Reliance Fixed Percentage 
Allocator) X the Zonal Grid Reliance Demand Adjustment Ratio. 
Where: 
The Zonal Network Integration Transmission Service Rate shall equal the rate for Network 
Integration Transmission Service set forth in Attachment H for the Zone with which the Co-
Located Load is interconnected, stated in dollars per megawatt per year. 
The Grid Reliance Charge Fixed Percentage Allocator shall be calculated as follows: 
The Grid Reliance Charge Fixed Percentage Allocator shall be a percentage value 
calculated as the average of all TO GRC Revenue Requirement Percentages 
TO GRC Revenue Requirement Percentage = TO GRC Revenue Requirement / TO Net 
Revenue Requirement 
TO GRC Revenue Requirement = [TO GRC Transmission O&M Percentage X TO 
Transmission O&M Expense] + [TO GRC Depreciation Expense] 
The TO GRC Transmission O&M Percentage shall be determined for each Transmission 
Owner in PJM for which FERC Form No. 1 account-level data is publicly available, and 
shall be equal to the amounts in FERC accounts 561-564 and 570-572 set forth in the 
Transmission Owner’s most recently published FERC Form No. 1, divided by the

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 11 of 17 
Transmission Owner’s transmission operations and maintenance amount contained in its 
most recently published FERC Form No. 1. 
The TO GRC Transmission O&M Expense shall be determined for each Transmission 
Owner in PJM, and is equal to the transmission operations and maintenance expense 
portion of the Transmission Owner’s revenue requirement determined based on its 
Attachment H formula rate template, as published in its most recent annual update. 
The TO GRC Depreciation Expense shall be determined for each Transmission Owner in 
PJM and shall be equal to the transmission depreciation expense portion of the 
Transmission Owner’s revenue requirement determined based on its Attachment H formula 
rate template, as published in its most recent annual update. 
The TO GRC Revenue Requirement Percentage shall be determined for each Transmission 
Owner in PJM and shall be equal to the Transmission Owner’s GRC Revenue Requirement 
divided by the Transmission Owner’s net transmission revenue requirement determined 
based on its Attachment H formula rate template, as published in its most recent annual 
update. 
The Grid Reliance Fixed Percentage Allocator shall initially be calculated as of the effective date 
of this Schedule, and will be published on the Transmission Provider’s website.   
The Grid Reliance Fixed Percentage Allocator will be updated by the Transmission Provider 
beginning with the first January 1 falling after the fifth anniversary of the effective date and every 
subsequent fifth anniversary of the most recent update thereafter.  No later than November 1 prior 
to the update effective date, each Transmission Owner will provide to the Transmission Provider 
the information required to determine the Grid Reliance Fixed Percentage Allocator.  No later than 
the following December 1, the Transmission Provider shall post on its website and in an 
information filing with FERC, the updated Grid Reliance Fixed Percentage Allocator including 
the information used to determine the Grid Reliance Fixed Percentage Allocator.  The updated 
Grid Reliance Charge for each Transmission Owner will become effective on the same date that 
its Network Integrated Transmission Service Charge is updated in the year following the update 
of the Grid Reliance Fixed Percentage Allocator.  
The Zonal Grid Reliance Demand Adjustment Ratio shall be calculated as the ratio of the Zonal 
demand used to determine Network Integration Transmission Service and Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service rates to the sum of this Zonal demand amount plus the Co-Located Gross 
Demand in excess of Firm Contract Demand for all Co-Located Load being served by Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service in the Zone. 
2)  
For Zones in which Transmission Owners charge for Network Integrated Transmission 
Service is not based on a formula rate, the Grid Reliance Charge shall be specified in a separate 
rate schedule to be filed by the Zonal Transmission Owner and to be effective on the same date as 
this Schedule [GRC] and updated each time such Transmission Owner updates its Network 
Integrated Transmission Service charge.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 12 of 17 
3) 
Revenues collected from Grid Reliance Charges shall be credited to Eligible Customers 
taking Network Integration Transmission Service, Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, 
and Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Service, based on each Eligible Customer’s pro rata share 
of the Zone’s annual peak load from the most recent 12-month period ending October 31.  The 
sum of these revenue credits will appear as a reduction to the gross monthly rate for service on an 
Eligible Customer’s bill in that month.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 13 of 17 
SCHEDULE [FP] 
Financial Penalty Charge for  
Unreserved Use by Co-Located Load 
An Eligible Customer taking Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service, or Interim Network Integration Transmission Service on behalf of 
Co-Located Load shall be subject to financial penalties for its unreserved use of the transmission 
system. 
The financial penalty charge for unreserved use shall include two components: (1) a base penalty 
charge, which applies to each individual hour in which the reserved transmission service limit is 
exceeded, and (2) a penalty ratchet, which applies when such exceedances occur repeatedly. 
Base Penalty Charge 
When an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Co-Located Load exceeds its reserved 
transmission service limit, a base penalty charge shall be assessed for any hour in which at least 
one five-minute interval occurs during which the Eligible Customer’s telemetered load at the Point 
of Delivery exceeds its reserved transmission service limit.  This five-minute interval is defined as 
an Exceedance Interval, and such an hour is defined as an Exceedance Hour.  The base penalty 
charge shall apply to each Exceedance Hour.   
For an Eligible Customer taking only Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, the 
reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service minus any curtailed MW.   
For an Eligible Customer taking only Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, 
the reserved transmission service limit shall equal the approved Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service minus any curtailed MW.   
For an Eligible Customer taking Firm Contract Demand and Non-Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Services, the reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service plus the approved Non-Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service minus any curtailed MW.   
For an Eligible Customer taking Interim Network Integration Transmission Service, the 
reserved transmission service limit shall equal the Interim Network Integration 
Transmission Service demand minus any curtailed MW. 
Each five-minute interval beginning with the first minute of each hour shall constitute a 
separate interval and each hour from 0100 through 2400 shall constitute a separate hour for 
purposes of determining whether one or more exceedances have occurred.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 14 of 17 
The base penalty charge shall be applied to each Exceedance Hour and shall be calculated as: 
Hourly Exceedance MW × Equivalent Hourly Firm Contract Demand (“FCD”) rate × 
number of Exceedance Intervals within the hour 
Where: 
Hourly Exceedance MW = Maximum telemetered load during the hour – Reserved 
Transmission Service Limit for the hour 
Equivalent Hourly FCD rate = FCD rate / 8,760 hours 
Penalty Ratchet 
A penalty rachet shall apply when multiple Exceedance Hours occur during a particular time period 
in order to escalate the penalty charges as the frequency of unreserved transmission use increases.   
If more than one Exceedance Hour occurs on the same calendar day, an additional daily 
penalty shall apply.   
If exceedances occur on multiple calendar days within the same calendar week, an 
additional weekly penalty shall apply.  
If exceedances occur in multiple calendar weeks within the same calendar month, an 
additional monthly penalty shall apply. 
If exceedances occur in multiple calendar months within the same calendar year, an 
additional yearly penalty shall apply.   
The penalty ratchet shall be based on an Eligible Customer’s exceedance pattern and applies 
escalating FCD-equivalent rates as the frequency of unreserved transmission use increases.  
Depending on whether exceedances occur within the same calendar day, calendar week, calendar 
month, or calendar year, the penalty ratchet shall apply daily, weekly, monthly, or annual penalty 
charges, respectively, as follows:  
Exceedance Pattern 
 
Penalty Rate Applied 
Multiple Exceedance Hours in a single calendar day  
Daily FCD-Equivalent Rate 
Multiple Exceedance Days within a calendar week  
Weekly FCD-Equivalent Rate 
Multiple Exceedance Weeks within a calendar month 
Monthly FCD-Equivalent Rate 
Multiple Exceedance Months within a calendar year  
FCD Annual Rate 
Daily Penalty Charge 
The Daily Penalty Charge is calculated as: 
Maximum Hourly Exceedance MW during the calendar day 
× Daily FCD Equivalent Rate 
× Number of Exceedance Hours in the calendar day

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 15 of 17 
Weekly Penalty Charge 
The Weekly Penalty Charge is calculated as: 
Maximum Hourly Exceedance MW during the calendar week 
× Weekly FCD Equivalent Rate 
× Number of Exceedance Days in the calendar week 
Monthly Penalty Charge 
The Monthly Penalty Charge is calculated as: 
Maximum Hourly Exceedance MW during the calendar month 
× Monthly FCD Equivalent Rate 
× Number of Exceedance Weeks in the calendar month 
Annual Penalty Charge 
The Annual Penalty Charge is calculated as: 
Maximum Hourly Exceedance MW during the calendar year 
× Annual FCD Rate 
× Number of Exceedance Months in the calendar year 
Revenues collected from Financial Penalty Charges shall be credited to Eligible Customers taking 
Network Integration Transmission Service and Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service.  The 
Transmission Provider shall return revenues collected from Financial Penalty Charges on a 
monthly and annual basis as bill credits to Eligible Customers taking Network Integration 
Transmission Service and Firm Contact Demand Service, who were not assessed Financial Penalty 
Charges during the year based on each Eligible Customer’s pro rata share of the Zone’s annual 
peak load based on the most recent 12-month period ending October 31.  The Eligible Customer’s 
pro rata share shall be based on the ratio of its Zone Network Load or Firm Contract Demand 
Transmission Service Amount to the sum of Network Customer Loads in the Zone and Firm 
Contract Demand Transmission Service Amounts for all Eligible Customers taking Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service in the Zone, for the applicable peak period.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 16 of 17 
Redlines to PJM OATT, Schedule 12
SCHEDULE 12 
Transmission Enhancement Charges 
*** 
(viii) FERC Filing. Within 30 days of the approval of each Regional Transmission 
Expansion Plan or an addition to such plan by the PJM Board pursuant to Operating Agreement, 
Schedule 6, section 1.6, the Transmission Provider shall designate in the Tariff, Schedule 12-
Appendix A and in a report filed with the FERC the Responsible Customers customers using Point-
to-Point Transmission Service and/or Network Integration Transmission Service and Merchant 
Transmission Facility owners that will be subject to each such Transmission Enhancement Charge 
(“Responsible Customers”) based on the cost responsibility assignments determined pursuant to 
this Schedule 12. Those customers designated by the Transmission Provider as Responsible 
Customers shall have 30 days from the date the filing is made with the FERC to seek review of 
such designation. Such cost responsibility designations shall be the same as those made for the 
relevant Regional Facility, Necessary Lower Voltage Facility, or Lower Voltage Facility in the 
Regional Transmission Expansion Plan.

Exhibit No. PTO-0006 
Page 17 of 17 
Redlines to PJM OATT, Part I, Section 1 (Definitions)
Responsible Customer: 
“Responsible Customer” shall mean customers using Interim Network Integration Transmission 
Service, Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, Non-Firm Contract Demand Transmission 
Service, Point-to-Point Transmission Service and/or Network Integration Transmission Service 
and Merchant Transmission Facility owners, which are assigned cost responsibility for 
Transmission Enhancement Charges as determined pursuant to Tariff, Schedule 12. 
Co-Located Gross Demand: 
“Co-Located Gross Demand” consists of the gross demand for a Co-Located Load facility, as 
specified in the applicable Service Agreement Contract Demand Transmission Service for Co-
Located Load.
